data.title: Bug: logical-assignment-operators never autofix introduces a setter call on a short-circuited assignment
data.titleHTML: Bug: logical-assignment-operators never autofix introduces a setter call on a short-circuited assignment
data.bodyHTML:
Environment

ESLint 10.10.0 and main commit 45ad79e; Node 22.23.2; Ubuntu.

Parser

Default (Espree).

What did you do?

const { Linter } = require("eslint");
const vm = require("node:vm");
const code = "var log=[];Object.defineProperty(globalThis,'p',{get(){return 1;},set(v){log.push('set');},configurable:true}); p ||= 2; log.join(',');";
const result = new Linter().verifyAndFix(code, {
  languageOptions: { ecmaVersion: 2022, sourceType: "script" },
  rules: { "logical-assignment-operators": ["error", "never"] }
});
console.log(JSON.stringify(vm.runInNewContext(code)));
console.log(JSON.stringify(vm.runInNewContext(result.output)));

What did you expect?

Both executions should return "": the truthy getter result makes the original assignment short-circuit without calling the setter.

What actually happened?

The fix changes p ||= 2 to p = p || 2, introducing an unconditional setter call. The executions return:

""
"set"

The same effect was reproduced with ??=. These observations use fresh Node VM contexts in script mode.

Link to Minimal Reproducible Example

ESLint Playground

AI acknowledgment

GPT-6 Astra assisted; I manually reviewed this report.

node.body:
In case of global variables, we could convert autofixes to suggestions, like we are already doing with member expressions for the same reason (possible setter). However, global setters seems like an extreme edge case, so I think we shouldn't make any changes to the rule.

@eslint/eslint-team thoughts?
node.bodyHTML:

@eslint/eslint-team thoughts?

This comment was created with AI (Claude Sonnet 5).

I dug into the root cause and have a fix ready, but per ESLint's AI contribution policy I understand AI-generated PRs are only considered for issues labeled accepted, so I'm posting the diagnosis and proposed fix here rather than opening a PR against an unaccepted issue. Happy to submit it as a PR if a maintainer marks this accepted.

Root cause

In lib/rules/logical-assignment-operators.js, the never-mode fixer (and the three always-mode fixers going the other direction) gate whether to auto-fix vs. only suggest via cannotBeGetter(node):

function cannotBeGetter(node) {
	return (
		node.type === "Identifier" &&
		(isStrict || !isInsideWithBlock(node))
	);
}

The intent is "a plain Identifier target can't have observable getter/setter side effects unless we're inside a non-strict with block." That's true for identifiers bound to local variables, but not for identifiers that resolve to an implicit global - i.e. no local declaration, so at runtime the reference is effectively a property access on the global object. In sourceType: "script", Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'p', { get, set, configurable: true }) makes plain p an accessor, with no with block involved at all, which is exactly this issue's repro.

isInsideWithBlock catches the with case; nothing catches the implicit-global case, so cannotBeGetter returns true (safe to auto-fix) when it shouldn't.

Proposed fix

The file already has the right tool for this: astUtils.isReferenceToGlobalVariable(scope, node) (used a few lines up, for detecting bare undefined) returns true exactly for a reference with no local declaration - which is precisely "could be an implicit-global accessor." Extending cannotBeGetter to take the enclosing scope and exclude that case:

function cannotBeGetter(node, scope) {
	return (
		node.type === "Identifier" &&
		!astUtils.isReferenceToGlobalVariable(scope, node) &&
		(isStrict || !isInsideWithBlock(node))
	);
}

This needs threading a scope (via sourceCode.getScope(...), same pattern already used for the IfStatement handler) through to all four call sites (never-mode AssignmentExpression, always-mode foo = foo || bar, always-mode foo || (foo = bar), and always-mode if (foo) foo = bar), since all four convert between forms that are only equivalent when the assignment target has no observable write side effect - the never direction currently over-fixes by adding an unconditional write, and the always direction under-fixes in the same way in reverse (removes a write that should stay conditional).

A variable that is locally declared (function param, let/const/var inside a function, etc.) is unaffected - isReferenceToGlobalVariable only returns true when reference.resolved.defs.length === 0, so the common case still auto-fixes exactly as it does today.

I verified this fix (and confirmed the bug reproduces without it) against the exact repro in this issue, plus checked all four cannotBeGetter call sites individually with both a global-identifier case (downgrades from autofix to suggestion-only, as intended) and a locally-scoped identifier case (still autofixes, no regression).

node.body: Based on the thumbs-up on my previous comment, it looks like the team agrees not to make any changes to this rule in this regard.
